steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: I feel... New. Complete.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Hahaha, you can stop circling me now, little fella. I'm just as happy to see you good as new.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Zumama: skilled at overhauls.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Zumama, requesting favor. Small favor.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: 0428, partner: already retired. No longer responding to communication. Requesting assistance.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Shipped along with this machine, built in the same factory. Now, no longer responding.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: No longer responding?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Don't worry. Take me to see it.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Zumama, this way.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: These components, and this design... Hmm, might be a bit more complicated than routine maintenance.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: How does this thing work? And what's this component for? It's nothing like Lancet, and I don't think Closure has ever said anything about these.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: If I connect it here... No, I should be more careful. This is your friend after all, right?

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Friend? Zumama has described this relationship several times. But I do not understand it.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Repair cannot be performed?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: If only I had some information to work from...

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Information? The library, preserves information.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Can you take me there?

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Assisting in navigation is my glorious mission. Zumama, this way please.

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: Now that's something you don't see every day.

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: I've never heard of anything like that in the books. Surface-dwellers are worth looking into.

steps.name: Inebriated Durin
steps.text: Elysium, let's have a little race to see who can fly out face-first from the super spinny slide the fastest. How about it?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Hah, you're about to see why they call me Rhodes Island's Legendary Aqua-Man!

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Thorns has nothing on me when it comes to this game!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I'll be honest here. I don't have the slightest bit of interest in hanging out with you. I'd rather be eaten by one of the gloompincers in that damned Acahuallan jungle.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Don't be like that, Stitch. I just want to hear your opinion.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Regardless of what the people of Zeruertza think, I know who's truly worth their mettle in this town – and that includes both you and your teacher. You've earned it.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I've never seen anything like Zeruertza's breathtaking dome in any piece of Durin architectural literature. If you could...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: If that's what you want to talk to me about, I suggest we stop here before wasting any more of each other's time.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I know you're not so into my Great Aquapit's design. Same goes for the slide, and the fountain. None of them are exactly masterpieces.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But, Stitch, do you know what is I really want to design? Same as you, the dome right over our heads! We were competing over it for the longest time!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Haha, you've got some nerve saying that to my face. Are you trying to pick a fight?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: You and I make good rivals.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Hah! Good rivals? You sure think highly of me. Should we hug it out? Put our arms around each other and weep?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I'm serious, Stitch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I just want to know. Why did you give up on the dome renovation project a few years ago?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: You stopped submitting your designs to the referendums. You just quit. You couldn't have given up trying to win people over to your aesthetic?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Were you really fine with Master Finch's unannounced farewell? He's still your...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Stop talking down to me, Catch!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I just got bored. Tired of it all. Simple as that.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I got fed up with trying to pin all my ambitions on this broken dome, and trying to get the people here to vote for me.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I got fed up with peddling solutions against 'architects with dreams' like you. It's all completely pointless!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Listen up. That piece of junk over our heads, I don't care if it leaks or explodes or even if you vote to tear it down one day––

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I don't give a damn anymore. So do whatever the hell you want with it!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But that dome is your teacher's...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I'll say it again.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Don't!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Give!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: A!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Damn!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: *sigh*... Alright.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Stitch, I wanted to ask you to work with me. The two of us could've come up with a brand-new plan for the dome, which I'm sure the vast majority of people here would've agreed to.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But since you don't care about the dome anymore, I won't push you. I respect your decision.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But, could you give me a moment of your time and offer me some feedback about my ideas for renovating the dome? I'd like your advice as well.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I don't care–– Actually, let's just hear it first.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Really? I appreciate it!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: First, I think the whole thing should be more colorful.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Intricate geometric patterns can greatly add to the beauty of the dome, just like stained glass!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: The juxtaposition of yellow, green, red, and blue! We'll let the citizens of Zeruertza know a new kind of beauty when they cast their eyes up!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Day or night, the new dome will become the singular focal point of everyone's attention! It'll be the safe harbor everyone comes back to in their search for peace of mind!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: A great, dazzling gemstone!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: What do you think? From my perspective, it's a brilliant, innovative design. I'm really proud of it. But I'm ready to take your feedback seriously.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Catch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Had a change of heart already? Then, we'll be partners...

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: You're not laying a single finger on the dome. I'm going to do everything in my power to stop you.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Didn't you just say you didn't give a damn anymore, and I could do whatever I want?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I thought you just wanted to resurrect that shambling corpse. Or put it to rest permanently. That, I don't care about.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: But I will not allow you to desecrate it in this manner!

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Huh? This is entirely a product of my respect for the dome.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: No. No way in hell. I swear I'm going to beat that idea out of your head!

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Maintenance materials, library. Location: Sorted Archives, Area 59. Available bookshelf.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Is this the place?

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Affirmative.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Let me see... Hm, is this Durin text? I can't read it at all.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Reading. Book titles: 'The Durin: To the Surface and Back Again' and 'Fine Durin Liquor: 127 Commonly-Seen Brewing Methods.'

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Continuing search. New hits: 'Believe It Or Not! Super Crazy Durin Masterplans' 'Research on Cybernetics Information Theory Based on the Influence of Social Behavior'....

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Little fella, are you sure they have what we're looking for here?

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Probability: 42.377%. Durins rarely organize things.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Hmm, I can read some of the words over here.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: The issues of 'Stranger Things' on these three bookshelves are more than ten years old. This row is for Victorian books... and you even have Kazimierz's 'The Red Wine'?

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: We use them to learn different languages, cultures, and news from the surface.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I see. No wonder why there's hardly any communication barrier between us.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Is this a Durin-published magazine? 'Breaking News! Attack of the Self-Driving Cart!', order one magazine and get a prototype for free... So that's what all those gadgets zipping around outside are?

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: Croque seriously pushed her cart modification business, and sold those add-on booster packs throughout Zeruertza.

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: She said, 'everyone likes a bit of randomness,' but I don't really get it.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: But why is this in Sargonian?

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: In order to carry on the fine tradition of 'Stranger Things,' we decided that our own magazine should also be in Sargonian! It's how Durins think.

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: Are you looking for this book? 'Build Your Own Assistant Robot in 3 Seconds.'

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: That sounds like it could come in handy. Thank you.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: Deculture! 0429 says hello!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: You two know each other?

steps.name: Durin Passerby
steps.text: Hello, allow me to introduce myself. I am Deculture Silvermint, the industry representative of Zeruertza.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: And also administrator of the assistant robots.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: The administrator...

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: That's right. The assistant robots in Zeruertza are built, supervised, and governed by me.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Model R3-E3 Assistant Robot #0429, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: This unit, submitted a request to Zumama. Overhaul 0428.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: 0428 has already been retired. Now return to your post.

steps.name: Strange Machine #0429
steps.text: ...Acknowledged. Executing directive.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Zumama, your communication with that assistant robot is pretty unusual, and its responses have been... abnormal.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: What's unusual about our communication?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: I can't say for sure. Maybe what's unusual is... the communication itself?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: You don't talk to the little fellas?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: No... They were made just to work.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: That's no good. I talk to my Lancet all the time. She's like a big sister to me, letting me lean up against her cold, metal shell, patting me on the shoulder with her robotic arm, singing to me with her beautiful synth...

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: 'Stranger Things' never mentioned anything like that.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Hehe, that was worth the trip!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I wasn't able to find the right outfit, but these little trinkets are awesome! Ores I've never seen before, these strange metal wind chimes, as well as these cute little pendants...

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: And most importantly! Gavial helped me pick this out...

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: The only thing that could be better is if Gavial bought a matching set with me!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Is she alright?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh, yeah, it's fine. The kid's been like that ever since she was little.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I've read that this obsessive hoarding behavior is called 'Zalak's Disease' in some places. It might be stress-induced or something.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: No, no, I'm really happy! These memories are very precious to me!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Okay, if you say so.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So, Avdotya, you have an Ursus name. Is that where you came from originally?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: My name is Avdotya Razorpen. A standard Durin name.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But, Avdotya is still Ursine.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: What are you getting at?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Calm down, I'm just making small talk.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: No... that place is not my home. I just happened to come from there.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What I really don't understand is why you're so paranoid about the surface.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: When I was little, I loved spending time with the grammar tutor my parents hired for me. Though she could be a bit dry, she sometimes said really interesting things.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Ursus has a lot of literature describing one's hometown, and my tutor was always entranced by those works. We would analyze their motifs, their composition styles...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Back then, I thought everyone would grow nostalgic for their hometown, and people who traveled far away would eventually find their way back to slumber eternally...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But I later found out that's not true at all. If all the memories you have of your hometown are painful ones, and you find a place more suitable to be your home, then why should you yearn for a place you once were?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: It is no different from another stop on a long journey.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Miss Avdotya, what made you decide to leave Ursus?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: ...I don't want to talk about it.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Things that would make you vomit. My status, my family, my friends, all vanished overnight. I fled with my tail between my legs, quite literally.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: From Ursus, to Sargon, to an underground Durin city... Your journey couldn't have been easy.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: How could there be a journey with no destination?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I just happened to get lucky. I finally found this place, a small city called Zeruertza.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The Durins here accepted me, and I will repay the debt with even greater kindness.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: This is the place I've decided I belong.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And that's why I won't let anything harm them. I don't care if it's out of malice, or out of good intentions gone awry.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: That is my warning to you.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I was going to ask you to have a drink, just as a show of goodwill. But maybe not––

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: That isn't off the table.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: ––Ahhh.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah. The way you drink definitely screams Ursus.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Shut up. Durins drink the same way.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: To be honest, I'm not much of a psychologist. There are a lot of things I don't understand about the human heart, and I don't really care to understand it. It's already hard enough patching up the body.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But what I can say is, you can never really become a Durin, no matter how much you act like one.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I don't think we know each other well enough to start picking out each others' problems.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I overheard you talking with some of those Durin shopkeepers. The gist I got was that the stories you wrote about snowfields didn't seem to strike the right note with them.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: That's right... They have neither snow nor fields underground.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Just to be clear, I don't write like that because I miss being there. It's nothing more than... a plot of land for a story to take place on.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You know that there's a story to be told there. That by itself isn't Durin.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Some scars can't be covered up after all.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But that won't stop me from trying.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Even if you just be yourself, the Durins will still accept you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: What if I want a new self?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Sure, the Durins are always happy to accept anyone they meet. This time, it was you people, and me. What about next time?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Since you are a doctor, you must have seen the evil lurking in men's hearts. You've surely seen the depravity to which people will stoop in order to hurt one another.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I won't act like this is a racial issue. Everything on the surface has shaped us into this. All too quick to resort to violence, lusting after power and money, blinded by ambition...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I used to be soaked in it. Now, I want a new self.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Evil is contagious, and can be learned. The people underground have never experienced it, and have no resistance to evil.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You're right, I can't become a Durin. But for the sake of the people of Zeruertza, I am willing to do everything in my power to protect it.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: ––I will protect this idyllic, unspoiled innocence.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Didn't you say before that the Durins can handle their own problems?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Stop using my own words against me!
